01.code-exec

CRITICAL1▾

Vulnerability description

JavaScript bridge parameter reaches Runtime.exec / ProcessBuilder

Remediation

Treat shared/external storage as untrusted: do not load executable or plugin code from it, verify APK integrity before any dynamic load, and scope read/write access with scoped-storage APIs rather than broad legacy permissions.

CWE · References

CWE-427Android Arbitrary Code Execution Via Third Party Package Contexts — oversecured.com ↗

Instances

  • CRITICALJavaScript bridge data reaches command execution❯
    com.securoid.ActionBridge#run(18 args)first-party1 path

02.webview

CRITICAL7▾

Vulnerability description

Attacker-controlled content is loaded into a WebView (loadUrl) — phishing or content injection risk without stronger WebView-specific evidence

Remediation

Do not load attacker-controlled URLs or content into a WebView. Restrict loadUrl/postUrl inputs to an allow-list of trusted origins, disable JavaScript and file access (setAllowFileAccess, setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs, setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs) unless strictly required, and avoid exposing @JavascriptInterface bridges to untrusted content.

CWE · References

CWE-79Android Security Checklist Webview — oversecured.com ↗

03.file

HIGH1▾

Vulnerability description

JavaScript bridge parameter reaches a file-write operation

Remediation

Canonicalize and validate every externally-influenced path before file access (File.getCanonicalPath + prefix check against a trusted base directory). Reject traversal sequences, use app-internal storage for sensitive files, and never delete or overwrite files outside the intended directory based on untrusted names.

CWE · References

CWE-22Path Traversal — developer.android.com ↗

Instances

  • HIGHJavaScript bridge data reaches file write❯
    com.securoid.ShareBridge#writeFile(36 args)first-party2 paths

04.redirection

HIGH5▾

Vulnerability description

Limited Intent Redirection — an Intent reconstructed from an attacker-controlled URI via Intent.parseUri/parseIntent is forwarded to a dispatch API; the parse constrains what the caller can express, which is weaker control than a directly attacker-supplied Intent

Remediation

Validate any externally-supplied Intent or URI before dispatching it. Prefer explicit component addressing (setPackage/setClass), reject or sanitize embedded intents, and never forward attacker-controlled extras into privileged dispatch APIs. Restrict exported components to the minimum surface the feature requires.

CWE · References

CWE-940Interception Of Android Implicit Intents — oversecured.com ↗
